chunks.subject: AP English Language
chunks.title: Argument exemplar — Sample 3A, score 1-4-1 (6/6)
chunks.content: Argument essay (Gorman, optimism vs. pessimism) scored 6/6 (Thesis 1, Evidence & Commentary 4, Sophistication 1). Thesis (1): defensible, nuanced position framing pessimism as a catalyst for optimism rather than its opposite. Evidence & Commentary (4): specific evidence for all claims (Cormac McCarthy's The Road; 'the coast' motif); commentary consistently explains how the evidence supports the reasoning about duality of thought. Sophistication (1): employs a consistently vivid and persuasive style from the opening ('two sides of the same coin') through the glass metaphor in the final paragraph.

chunks.subject: AP English Language
chunks.title: Argument exemplar — Sample 3B, score 1-3-0 (4/6)
chunks.content: Argument essay scored 4/6 (Thesis 1, Evidence & Commentary 3, Sophistication 0). Thesis (1): defensible position that optimism and pessimism are not opposites and balance is essential. Evidence & Commentary (3): specific evidence for all three claims (The Lost Hero, Leo's invention); commentary explains how some evidence supports a claim — but some commentary (paragraph 3) does not clearly connect to the claim that optimism and pessimism are not opposites, so short of 4. Sophistication (0): not demonstrated.

chunks.subject: AP English Language
chunks.title: Argument exemplar — Sample 3C, score 1-2-0 (3/6)
chunks.content: Argument essay scored 3/6 (Thesis 1, Evidence & Commentary 2, Sophistication 0). Thesis (1): defensible position that Gorman's claim is invalid. Evidence & Commentary (2): relevant evidence, some specific (a pessimist friend) mixed with broad generalities; commentary explains how some evidence relates to the argument but does not connect it to a claim, so no clear line of reasoning; makes one point well but not multiple supporting claims. Sophistication (0): not demonstrated.
